idiom_name: readonly snapshots (Readonly<T>, readonly T[], as const) + structural sharing; the runtime is JavaScript's
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds the enforcement layer to JavaScript's mechanics: Readonly<Type> 'constructs a type with all properties of Type set to readonly, meaning the properties of the constructed type cannot be reassigned' - the docs point at Object.freeze for the runtime equivalent - while readonly T[]/ReadonlyMap keep the writer's own code from mutating the snapshot, and a discriminated-union state type makes 'build a new snapshot' the only legal update form. The runtime behaviour is unchanged (shallow spreads, structural sharing, no shared object graph between agents), so the thread-safety notes are JavaScript's: one owner per snapshot, message passing between agents, and Atomics only over SharedArrayBuffer. A counted body remains inexpressible without native/WebAssembly code; the types only make the immutability discipline checkable.
pitfalls: Readonly<T> is erased and shallow: it stops reassignment in type-checked code, not mutation of nested objects or of the aliased value at runtime - freeze the same objects the type describes.

ReadonlyMap/ReadonlySet are compile-time views: the underlying Map is still mutable if any code holds the mutable type, so a snapshot that must stay stable has to be copied (new Map(m)) at the boundary, not just retyped.

Structural sharing makes identity a poor probe: unchanged subtrees keep the same reference after a spread (good for memoisation, useless as a 'did this change?' test), while a nested object mutated in place keeps its identity although its contents changed.
sources: TypeScript documentation, Utility Types - Readonly<Type> makes properties non-reassignable and points at Object.freeze for the runtime form: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/utility-types.html

MDN, Atomics - the only genuinely shared-memory primitives available to the runtime, restricted to SharedArrayBuffer/ArrayBuffer views: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Atomics
